notes: Site: headless Shopify behind Next.js/Vercel. Access: plain HTTP GET, desktop UA, no WAF, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Navigation discovery: full mega-menu (11 top-level nodes, see bs218.json notes) has no Clearance/Outlet/Sale node. Homepage's own RSC-rendered merchandising sections are only 'Bestsellers' and 'New Launches' - no Sale/Clearance section is promoted on the homepage at all. Grepped sitemap.xml (486 URLs) for sale/clear/outlet/final/last-chance/end-of-line/discontinued and found three live-looking handles: sale-nw, republic-day-sale-up-to-40-off-sitewide, flashsale. Also directly probed plausible clearance-style handles not present in the sitemap (/collections/clearance, /outlet, /end-of-line, /last-chance, /final-sale, /outlet-sale, /clearance-sale) - all 7 returned the site's genuine not-found/empty state (no 'initialProducts' key present at all in the RSC payload, distinct from a live-but-empty collection), so none of those exist. Of the three sitemap hits: republic-day-sale-up-to-40-off-sitewide and flashsale both resolve to live routes but their initialProducts.edges arrays are empty (0 products) - these are expired/emptied named seasonal campaigns (Republic Day is a specific Indian public holiday, i.e. inherently a time-boxed promotional event, not clearance/outlet) - dropped per the zero-product rule and would have been excluded as generic seasonal promotions regardless per the Sale-vs-Clearance test. /collections/sale-nw is live and populated: initialProducts.pageInfo.hasNextPage=false with 52 distinct gid://shopify/Product IDs (real PLP: product grid + price/colour/size facets, not editorial). However this page's own title/handle is simply 'sale' - grepped the entire page (all ~766KB) for clearance/outlet/final sale/end of line/last chance/discontinued and found zero genuine occurrences (the one 'Outlet' hit is a React component name 'OutletBoundary', a Next.js internal, not page copy). The page is also not linked from the current homepage or mega-menu (only reachable via sitemap/direct URL), unlike bestseller-nw and new-launch-new which ARE homepage-promoted. Per the brief's Clearance-vs-Sale test: the site's own taxonomy gives no permanence signal (no 'outlet', 'final', 'end of line', 'last chance', 'discontinued' wording anywhere), so this cannot be confidently classified as genuine Clearance-style merchandising rather than a temporary/rotating sitewide discount page - especially since the site is independently shown to run named, time-boxed sale campaigns (Republic Day Sale) that later go empty, suggesting 'sale-nw' could be a similar rotating campaign under a generic evergreen handle. Recording it with a MANUAL REVIEW flag per brief instructions rather than silently including or excluding it. No non-English content encountered.
